source_text: Studies in voluntary medical male circumcision programs in sub-Saharan Africa indicate that perceived norms favoring circumcision correlate with reduced anticipated stigma for participants, suggesting that widespread adoption aligns individuals with dominant social expectations and averts marginalization. [104]
